description: Cases for the size-split sub-issue trust rule (admit.mjs splitChildBody, its one home; owner Q93 with the Q9 extension): a body counts as the listed human's text only when the lanes App wrote it, its native parent was filed by a listed human, its header names that parent, and either nobody edited it and every line after the header is a line of the parent's trusted text, or a listed human last edited it (a ticked task box is an edit), which makes it that human's text. An edit by any other account leaves it untrusted. A header whose third line is `<!-- size-split refinement=<id> updated_at=<time> -->` (its part line then reads "copied from #N and intake's refinement comment on it as written") also allows the lines of that comment, and counts at all only while that comment is still the parent's newest refinement (the lanes App's comment opening with `<!-- intake-triage refinement -->`), never edited (last_edited_at null), with updated_at equal to its created_at or to the recorded time, on a parent body a listed human wrote; this holds even when a listed human edited the child. Actors are {type, id} with type User or Bot; parent is the child's native parent number or null; size is the triage Size. admit.test.mjs and resolve-pr.test.mjs read this file. child.parent is null or {number, repo}, repo as owner/name and absent for this repository; a parent elsewhere never counts. A parent's comments, oldest first, are {id, author, body, created_at, updated_at, last_edited_at, editor}, id the REST and GraphQL databaseId. A case-level app_id overrides the top-level one, and null means the reader has no lanes App id, so nothing counts.
